clue.text: Two male animals stiffening

parts.note: a buck is a male deer or rabbit
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Two males of the herd going rigid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two male animals' gives two pieces, a buck and a ram, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is coarse cloth treated with glue and used as a stiffener in bookbinding and tailoring.

clue.text: Dry in the piece and cut in half

indicators.note: in places the word for dry inside the word for piece

parts.note: a bit is a piece
sec is French for dry, used of wine

explanation.surface: Instructions to dry a piece of food and slice it down the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: SEC, the wine term for dry, sits inside BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to divide into two equal parts.

clue.text: Up which Newbolt's Drake would drum the Dons

definitions.text: Up which Newbolt's Drake would drum the Dons

parts.words: Up which Newbolt's Drake would drum the Dons
parts.note: alludes to the poem Drake's Drum, in which Drake promises to drum the Spaniards up the stretch of sea between England and France

explanation.surface: A literary quiz question about Newbolt's poem.
explanation.walkthrough: In Henry Newbolt's poem Drake's Drum, Drake vows to return and 'drum them up the' waterway 'as we drummed them long ago'; the Dons are Spaniards, not Oxford lecturers.
explanation.definitionFit: The English Channel is the strait where the Spanish Armada was harried in 1588.

clue.text: Terse, sour, mixed-up characters turned up

indicators.note: mixed-up says the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A description of curt, sullen, confused people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed-up' rearranges TERSE SOUR; 'characters' just means letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Retroussé describes a nose that is tilted upward at the tip.

clue.text: The size of certain fellows seen in the flesh!

indicators.note: seen in puts the pieces for certain fellows within the word for flesh

parts.note: meat is flesh
sure means certain
men are fellows

explanation.surface: A remark on how big some men look in the nude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in the flesh' sounds like meeting in person; it puts SURE MEN inside MEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A measurement is a dimension, such as size or extent.

clue.text: The traveller is soft, the Italian unyielding

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for soft
il is Italian for 'the'
grim can mean stern and unyielding

explanation.surface: A character sketch of a wanderer who is gentle while his Italian companion is hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Italian' is not a person but the Italian word for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrim is someone who makes a journey to a holy place, a kind of wayfarer.

clue.text: Step back in disappointment

indicators.note: back says the letters found are to be read in the opposite direction
in says the letters are found inside the word disappointment

explanation.surface: Taking a step back when let down.
explanation.walkthrough: SAP lies within 'disappointment'; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A pas is a step in ballet.

clue.text: The shortest is Meadow Street

parts.note: a lea is a meadow, a poetic word

explanation.surface: Naming the stubbiest road in town.
explanation.walkthrough: LEA (meadow) plus ST (street); 'is' links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Least means smallest, or of the lowest amount.

clue.text: More inclined to fall in behind

indicators.note: in puts the word for fall inside the word for behind

parts.note: the rear is the behind
to fall in battle is to die

explanation.surface: Someone keener to slot in at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: DIE goes inside REAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Readier means more willing or prepared.

clue.text: Republic once arranged galas throughout the month

indicators.note: throughout has the month spread around the jumbled galas

parts.note: May is a month

indicators.note: arranged shows the word galas is to be reordered

explanation.surface: A country that once held festivities all month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns GALAS into LAGAS, which goes inside MAY. Madagascar was once the Malagasy Republic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Malagasy Republic was the name of Madagascar from 1958 to 1975.

clue.text: So bishops move to confine many a worker within rules

indicators.note: within says the first pair of pieces sit inside the word for rules

parts.note: to sway is to rule or hold power over
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, crosswordese for many
an ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: Chess talk of diagonal bishops, slyly suggesting churchmen hemming a labourer in with regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to confine' and 'within' both point to the insertion of L and ANT into SWAYS. Bishops on a chessboard can only move diagonally.
explanation.definitionFit: Slantways means diagonally, which is the only direction a chess bishop may travel.

clue.text: A few are poorly but are of service

annotationWithheld.why: A few are poorly but are of service (5): 'are' gives A and 'poorly' AIL, but nothing in 'A few' fairly yields the V of AVAIL; the scan confirms 'few'.
annotationWithheld.clue: A few are poorly but are of service

clue.text: Some poetry's hypocrisy, nothing more

parts.note: cant is insincere, hypocritical talk
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A complaint that some verse is nothing but sanctimonious humbug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more' simply tacks the O on after CANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A canto is one of the main divisions of a long poem, such as Dante's Inferno.

clue.text: Like sun rising and vanishing — how disturbing!

parts.note: a sun that has risen is up
the sun vanishing below the horizon is setting

explanation.surface: Watching the sun come up and go down, someone finds the whole thing alarming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like sun' sets the scene for both pieces: a sun can be up and can be setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Upsetting means troubling or distressing.

clue.text: A youth-leader must score at break

indicators.note: break shows the words must score at are to be broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A youth worker has to hit the target during the break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' looks like a pause; it rearranges MUST SCORE AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoutmaster runs a troop of Boy Scouts.

clue.text: Building lists appear for moulding material

indicators.note: building suggests the words are being assembled into something new

explanation.surface: Construction lists show up for a casting compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' rearranges LISTS APPEAR FOR into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaster of Paris is a quick-setting gypsum paste used to make casts and moulds.

clue.text: Dividing £25, a tidy inheritance

indicators.note: dividing means the words a tidy split the sum of money in two

parts.note: a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds
trim means neat and tidy

explanation.surface: Splitting twenty-five pounds, a modest legacy.
explanation.walkthrough: A PONY is British slang for £25; A TRIM splits it.
explanation.definitionFit: Patrimony is property passed down from one's father or ancestors.

clue.text: One class takes in clothing to wash

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: takes in means the word for class encloses the word for clothing

parts.note: rate means class or grade, as in first-rate
rig is an outfit or clothing

explanation.surface: A school class taking in laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: I, then RATE taking in RIG.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrigate is to flush or supply with water.

clue.text: The portrayal of engineers setting forth

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
setting forth an argument is presenting it, a presentation

explanation.surface: A picture of engineers laying out their plans.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A representation is a depiction or portrayal of something.

clue.text: Sported at the seaside, with or without a canoe

definitions.text: Sported at the seaside, with or without a canoe

parts.words: Sported at the seaside, with or without a canoe
parts.note: describes wading in the shallows, or propelling a small boat with a blade

explanation.surface: Fun at the beach, boat optional.
explanation.walkthrough: One verb covers both: splashing about in shallow water and propelling a canoe.
explanation.definitionFit: To paddle is both to wade in shallow sea water and to row a canoe.

clue.text: There's nothing fixed about gold being substandard

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: about says the word for fixed goes around the heraldic gold

parts.note: fast means fixed firmly
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A remark that nothing about gold is reliably below par.
explanation.walkthrough: FAST goes about OR to make FASORT, after O. 'Of a sort' implies something mediocre.
explanation.definitionFit: Of a sort means of a poor or indifferent kind, so not up to par.

clue.text: Cut north to Sabrina's abode

parts.note: to sever is to cut
N is north

explanation.surface: Directions for going north to Sabrina's house.
explanation.walkthrough: In legend and Milton's Comus, Sabrina is the nymph of the River Severn in western England and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabrina, the river goddess of Milton's Comus, lives in the Severn, the Latin name for it being Sabrina.

clue.text: Something potted by Kipling in the East?

definitions.text: Something potted by Kipling in the East?

parts.words: Something potted by Kipling in the East?
parts.note: potted suggests summarised writing by the author of tales of India, but really means a leaf brewed in a pot out there

explanation.surface: Kipling's condensed tales of the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potted' plays on a potted (abridged) story and something put in a teapot; Kipling is famous for writing about British India.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea grown in Assam or Darjeeling is brewed in a pot, the subcontinent being where Kipling set much of his work.

clue.text: Man for instance is said to be part of the church

indicators.note: is said means a word is spoken, so we want a sound-alike

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an island

explanation.surface: A claim that a man is a component of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland; ISLE spoken matches the church passage.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage in a church between rows of pews.

clue.text: Picture that's one thousand years old?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
age is how many years old one is

explanation.surface: Is this painting a millennium old?
explanation.walkthrough: Two Roman numerals, I and M, are followed by AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a likeness or picture of something.

clue.text: A bull's heart is found in place of Iphigenia

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters, here the middle of bull

explanation.surface: A bull's heart found at a site from Greek myth, perhaps after a sacrifice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes the middle two letters, UL, of 'bull'. In Greek myth Agamemnon was to sacrifice his daughter Iphigenia at Aulis.
explanation.definitionFit: Aulis is the Boeotian port where the Greek fleet gathered and Iphigenia was offered to Artemis.

clue.text: Point to Bismarck, queer cove so it's whispered

parts.note: S (south) is a compass point
Otto von Bismarck was the German chancellor

indicators.note: queer, meaning odd, marks the letters of cove for rearranging

explanation.surface: A remark to Bismarck about a strange fellow, spoken in a hushed voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queer' rearranges COVE into VOCE, after S and OTTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Sotto voce is Italian for 'under the voice', meaning in an undertone.

clue.text: Message sent when holed amidships

parts.note: the distress call a ship sends when its hull is breached; also, a hole shape amid two ship abbreviations

explanation.surface: What a ship transmits after being holed in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: A holed ship sends the distress signal; cheekily, O (a hole) sits amid SS (steamship).
explanation.definitionFit: The Morse distress signal is broadcast by vessels in danger of sinking.

clue.text: Failing to come to any conclusion

definitions.text: Failing to come to any conclusion

parts.words: Failing to come to any conclusion
parts.note: reads like indecision but literally describes something lacking a finish

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an inconclusive debate; read literally it is something without an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no finish goes on forever, eternal or interminable.

clue.text: Absurd story about a place in Herts

indicators.note: absurd suggests the word story is nonsensical and needs reshaping

parts.note: on can mean about, concerning

explanation.surface: A far-fetched tale concerning a Hertfordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absurd' rearranges STORY into ROYST. Herts is Hertfordshire, an English county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Royston is a market town in north Hertfordshire.
